add_time.description: Shift a date by an amount and unit, like +3 days or -2 hours, or move it to a day of the week, like next Monday. Use a negative amount to go back in time. A date stays a date (three days after 2026-10-09 is 2026-10-12), and a time keeps its clock time across daylight saving changes. Handy for due dates, reminders, and expiry dates.
add_time.name: add_time

parameters.description: The starting date, like 2026-06-30, June 30, 2026 or 6/30/2026 9:30 AM.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: How much to shift the date by. Use a negative number to subtract, like -2 to go back two units. With a day of the week, 1 is the next one and -1 the last one.
parameters.name: amount

parameters.description: The unit of time to add or subtract, or a day of the week to move to, like next Monday.
parameters.name: unit

returns.description: The new date (2026-07-03) when you started from a date, otherwise the new date and time as an ISO 8601 timestamp in your time zone.

date_difference.description: Measure the time between two dates in a chosen unit (years, quarters, months, weeks, working days, days, hours, minutes, or seconds). Months, quarters and years count complete calendar months, so a start date of 2022-07-03 is 4 years before 2026-07-03; working days count Monday to Friday. Dates are read in your time zone. The result is signed: positive when the end date is after the start date, negative when it's before. Unlike the Time until date action, which counts from now, this measures between two dates you provide.
date_difference.display_str_template: Get the difference between {0} and {1} in {2}
date_difference.name: date_difference

parameters.description: The date to measure from, like 2026-06-30, June 30, 2026 or 6/30/2026 9:30 AM.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: The date to measure to, like 2026-06-30, June 30, 2026 or 6/30/2026 9:30 AM.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: The unit to measure the difference in.
parameters.name: unit

returns.description: The whole number of units from the start date to the end date, negative if the end date is earlier.

date_part.description: Pull a single component out of a date: the year, quarter, month, week of the year, day of the month, month and day together, day of the week, hour, or minute, read in your time zone. Returns a number for every part except day of the week, which returns the weekday name like Monday, and month and day, which returns text like 07-03. Use it for conditional logic on a date, such as acting only in December or only on the 1st, or compare the month and day of two dates to find anniversaries and birthdays.
date_part.name: date_part

parameters.description: The date to read from, like 2026-06-30, June 30, 2026 or 6/30/2026 9:30 AM.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: Which component of the date to extract.
parameters.name: part

returns.description: The part of the date (in your time zone) that was asked for: a number for the year, quarter, month, week, day of the year or month, hour, minute or second, the name for the month name and the day of the week, or MM-DD text for the month and day.

format_date.description: Turn a date into a friendly format for emails, messages, or reports.
format_date.name: format_date

parameters.description: The date to make readable, like 2026-06-30, June 30, 2026 or 6/30/2026 9:30 AM.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: How to show the date: a long date and time, just the date or the time, an ISO 8601 timestamp, how long ago or until it is, or your own pattern.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: How to write the date, using these codes: YYYY (2026), MMMM (July), MMM (Jul), MM (07), D (3), Do (3rd), dddd (Friday), ddd (Fri), h (4), HH (16), mm (30), A (PM). Other characters are written as they are, and text in [brackets] is never read as codes. For example, dddd, MMMM D gives Friday, July 3.
parameters.name: pattern

parameters.description: Which time zone to use, like America/New_York. Without one, it is your own time zone from Settings (UTC if you haven't set one).
parameters.name: timezone

parameters.description: How to read a date written in numbers, like 03/07/2026: the way people write dates in your country, or always day first or month first. Use this for dates that come from another country.
parameters.name: written_as

options.label: The way my country writes it

returns.description: The date as readable text, in the chosen format and time zone.

is_business_day.description: Check whether a date is a business day: a weekday that is not a public holiday.
is_business_day.display_str_template: Check if {0} is a business day
is_business_day.name: is_business_day

parameters.description: The date to check, like 2026-06-30.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: The country whose public holidays are skipped. Defaults to the United States.
parameters.name: region

returns.description: Whether the date is a weekday that is not a public holiday in the region.

is_holiday.description: Check whether a date is a public holiday.
is_holiday.name: is_holiday

parameters.description: The date to check, like 2026-06-30.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: The country whose public holidays count. Defaults to the United States.
parameters.name: region

returns.description: Whether the date is a public holiday in the region, or the weekday a weekend holiday is observed on.

is_weekend.description: Check whether a date falls on a weekend (Saturday or Sunday).
is_weekend.name: is_weekend

parameters.description: The date to check, like 2026-06-30.
parameters.name: date

returns.description: Whether the date falls on a Saturday or Sunday.

is_within.description: Check whether a date falls within the last or next few days, weeks or months, like an order from the last 7 days or a renewal in the next 30. Today counts.
is_within.display_name: Check if a date is recent or coming up
is_within.name: is_within

parameters.description: The date to check, like 2026-06-30.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: Look back from today, or ahead.
parameters.name: direction

parameters.description: How many, like 7 for the last 7 days.
parameters.name: amount

parameters.description: Days, weeks, months, and so on.
parameters.name: unit

returns.description: Whether the date is within that many days, weeks or months of today, today included.

now.description: Get the current date and time.
now.display_str_template: Get the current date and time
now.name: now

returns.description: The current date and time as an ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds, in your account's time zone.

period_edge.description: Get the first or last day of the week, month, quarter or year a date falls in, like the 1st of this month or the end of the quarter, or round a time down to the hour or minute.
period_edge.display_name: Start or end of a period
period_edge.name: period_edge

parameters.description: A date in the period, like today. For last month, go back a month with Add or subtract time first.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: The first or the last day of the period.
parameters.name: edge

parameters.description: Which period. Weeks run Monday to Sunday.
parameters.name: period

returns.description: The first or last day of the period (2026-07-01) when you started from a date, otherwise its first or last moment as an ISO 8601 timestamp in your time zone.

read_date.description: Read a date written in a particular way, like 15-10-26 14h30, or a time in another time zone, like 9:00 New York time, so other steps can use it.
read_date.name: read_date

parameters.description: The date or time as written, like 15-10-26 14h30.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: How it is written, in the codes “Make date readable” uses: DD-MM-YY HH[h]mm reads 15-10-26 14h30, DD/MM/YYYY reads 03/04/2026 as 3 April, and X reads a Unix timestamp. Text in [brackets] is matched as it is. Leave empty to read any usual way of writing a date.
parameters.name: pattern

parameters.description: The time zone a time written without one is in, like America/New_York. Without one, it is your own time zone from Settings.
parameters.name: timezone

returns.description: The date (2026-10-15), or the moment as an ISO 8601 timestamp with its time zone's offset, ready for any date step.

set_date_part.description: Change one part of a date and keep the rest, like 9:00 on the due date or the 15th of this month.
set_date_part.name: set_date_part

parameters.description: The date to change, like the due date or today.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: Which part of the date to set.
parameters.name: part

parameters.description: What to set it to: a time like 9:00 or 5:30 PM, a number like 15, or a month like March. A day past the end of the month is its last day.
parameters.name: value

returns.description: The changed date (2026-10-15), or, once it has a time, an ISO 8601 timestamp in your time zone.

time_until.description: Find out how many seconds remain until a date and time.
time_until.name: time_until

parameters.description: The moment to count down to. Pick it from the field, or reference a variable with @ to count down to a date and time an earlier step produced.
parameters.name: date

returns.description: The whole number of seconds from now until the date, negative if it has passed.

parameters.description: Which time zone to use, like America/New_York. Without one, it is your own time zone from Settings (UTC if you haven't set one).
parameters.name: timezone

returns.description: Today's date as YYYY-MM-DD, in the chosen time zone or your account's.

parameters.description: Which time zone to use, like America/New_York. Without one, it is your own time zone from Settings (UTC if you haven't set one).
parameters.name: timezone

returns.description: Tomorrow's date as YYYY-MM-DD, in the chosen time zone or your account's.

unix_timestamp.description: Get a date, or the current time, as a Unix timestamp: the number of seconds (or milliseconds) since January 1, 1970, the way many apps write dates.
unix_timestamp.name: unix_timestamp

parameters.description: The date and time to turn into a timestamp. Leave empty for now.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: Seconds, the usual choice, or milliseconds, which JavaScript and some apps use.
parameters.name: unit

returns.description: The moment as whole seconds (or milliseconds) since January 1, 1970 (UTC). A date without a time is the start of that day in your time zone.

weekday_name.description: Get the weekday for a date, like Monday or Saturday.
weekday_name.display_str_template: Get the day of the week for {0}
weekday_name.name: weekday_name

parameters.description: The date to look up, like 2026-06-30.
parameters.name: date

returns.description: The day of the week of the date in your time zone, such as Monday.

parameters.description: Which time zone to use, like America/New_York. Without one, it is your own time zone from Settings (UTC if you haven't set one).
parameters.name: timezone

returns.description: Yesterday's date as YYYY-MM-DD, in the chosen time zone or your account's.

description: Get, format, and compare dates and times.
